content.text: The web knows what an issue can edit; the agent cannot ask.
- The web write path does GET <key>/editmeta/ then PATCH <key>/fields/ (specs/000-product/contracts/api.md:368-388, internal/server/write.go:790-832).
- gadak edit --help is a fixed flag list. gadak fields is a site-wide custom-field usage report that requires a credential and queries Jira — not per-issue schema.
- MCP exposes five read tools and no write (internal/mcp/tools.go:29-34).
An agent that wants to change a field it has no flag for has no way to learn what is allowed, so it falls back to `gadak api --write` or gives up. That is the opposite of least surprise.

Fix shape: gadak issue KEY --editmeta --json printing {fields:[{alias,id,kind,required,options}]} from one origin round trip, intersected with the configured editable allowlist exactly as the web does (internal/fields/editable.go). No editmeta cache treated as a source of truth.
Gate: against a fake editmeta containing an option field, the CLI JSON lists that alias and omits ids outside the allowlist; with no credential it refuses the same way the web does.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track C, score 8/10).
